sentences.text: Thanks for making the time. What made you look at this now?
Everything I get out of the assistant reads like a press release. My team can tell in one line that I did not write it.
So the problem is the voice, not the facts.
Right. I have tried pasting in old posts, I have tried a custom GPT, and it still drifts back to generic within three replies.
How much of your own writing do you have to hand?
Years of it. Emails, decks, a newsletter. I do not know how much of that the model actually needs to learn me.
The other question I keep hitting is whether I should build my own skill for this or just buy something.
What would consistent look like for you?
The same voice in a two-line email, a LinkedIn post and a board deck, without me rewriting every draft from scratch.
That is what the compile step is for. It grades your own examples and only keeps rules your grading supports.

summary.overview: A senior operator wants an assistant that writes in their own voice; current tools drift to generic output and they are weighing building a personal skill against buying one.
